title: Q&A with Vasco Duarte on the #NoEstimates Book
summary: InfoQ interview with Vasco Duarte on the NoEstimates book: estimates fail and breed dysfunction, so plan by goals, forecast from delivery rate and manage scope continuously.

assertions.quote: Of the large systems that are completed, about 66% experience schedule delays & cost overrun
On-time, on-budget record is a poor predictor of project success.
additionally promote many different dysfunctions in the organization. In the book I explain some of those dysfunctions such as: estimate bargaining, political games
we can easily decide which stories to take into a sprint without sizing those stories
I project (forecast) the rate of delivery (delivered items divided by the time it took to deliver) into the future
many of the items of functionality we end up delivering to our customers are rarely or never used

verdicts.note: The widely cited 64% figure comes from a small Standish sample; feature usage is skewed but the magnitude is unknown.

assertions.quote: we discover value as we deliver what we had originally planned

verdicts.note: Requirements do emerge during development, but scope creep also includes gold-plating and unmanaged change, so treating all of it as value is optimistic.

assertions.quote: Let's not forget that estimation is not a technique developed for software projects.

verdicts.note: Unlike most studied professions where models beat experts, software expert estimates match or beat models because case-specific knowledge matters more and software size-effort models perform worse, so results from other domains transfer imperfectly.
